description:
Goal: Stop rebuilding and interning an activation-key arrow when closure-identity erasure has no DispatchDemand::Ignore parameter.

Authority: erase_transported_closure_identities alone owns this key transformation. A mask that leaves every parameter Whole cannot change the arrow, so the existing Ty is the proof; no descriptor cache or second equality authority.

TDD: first prove an all-Whole mask returns the exact input Ty and causes no raw interner probe, normalization, or insertion; prove an Ignore mask still erases a closure identity and returns the canonical transformed arrow. Exercise the enum_take_drop_split canonical fixture and record the direct reuse count.

Acceptance: focused type/canonical/fixture gates, docs explaining the identity law, format/check/strict Clippy, then one commit and close.

comments.text: Measured on exact fixtures2/behavior/enum_take_drop_split.fz, atop .48.13. An all-Whole local dispatch mask occurred 197 times: direct identity reuse rises 12,394 -> 12,591 and raw interner probes fall 126,171 -> 125,974. Normalizations (11,875) and unique inserts (1,033) are unchanged. This is precise no-op removal, not a descriptor cache.

title: Preserve arrow identity when closure erasure has no target
